idle: (He runs a thumb along a broken shaft.) Good grain on this one.
good_ice: Ice is like a good tabletop. Flat, and you notice when it isn't.
wet_ice: Wet. Like glue that's in a hurry.
cold: Cold's fine. Wood likes it steady.
hungry: Bev usually has a coffee going. I'll go see.
long_line: I'll wait. Glue waits. So can I.
bored: (He measures the armrest of his seat with his fingers.)
goal: Broke his stick on that one. I'll take it.
greet_owner: Afternoon. Barrel's filling up, I hear.
leaving_happy: Good night. Got three Kodiaks for the truck.
leaving_angry: I'll go back to my shop. It doesn't leak.

beer_league: There goes another stick. Wood, I hope.
senior_hockey: That's a Warlock he just broke. Forty-two.

first.say: Lorne Pettipiece. Woodworks, outside Harlow Falls. I buy Bev's broken sticks. Three dollars for wood, a dollar for composite, and I'm overpaying for the composite.

options.text: What do you make with them?
(Sit on the bench by the front doors.)

first_make.say: Coat racks. Benches. The odd Adirondack chair. That bench by your front doors is forty-one broken Warlocks.

first_sit.say: It's dry. Good. (A pause.) The new one in the truck isn't. I'll tell you when.

say: (He nods at the ice.) Number nine's stick won't last the period. Wood. Good.
Mm. What can I do for you?

options.text: What brings you to the rink?
Tell me about the Warlock bench.
What do you make of the building?
Could you take the stick barrel regularly?

job.say: A workshop with a house attached. Most days it's me, a plane and the radio. The radio does most of the talking.

events.say: Beer league, for the broken sticks. Lumber Kings, for the broken sticks and the hockey. A good dovetail and a good power play are the same thing. Everything fits.

options.text: Never thought of it that way.

gossip.say: Bev and I go back. She keeps the barrel, I keep her honest about composites. She says the bench is sturdier than the sticks ever were. She's right. She usually is.

gossip_penny.say: Wants skate aids for grown-ups out of broken sticks. Good idea. Six out of Honests is a Tuesday.

bench.say: Forty-one Warlocks, two winters of glue-ups and one argument with Bev about which way the grain runs. I won. She says she let me.

options.text: Could you make one for the stands someday?

bench_stands.say: Maybe. When the barrel's full. Wood doesn't rush and neither do I.

rink.say: Good bones. The old dressing room benches are real maple, which nobody builds with any more. The seats are a different story.

rink_better.say: Somebody's been careful in here. The joins are clean. I notice joins.

order.say: Every two weeks, I'll come for the barrel. Three a wooden shaft, a dollar a composite. Bev keeps the count. There's about twenty dollars in it today.

do.note: Lorne Pettipiece will take the broken-stick barrel every two weeks: $3 a wooden shaft, $1 a composite.

order_yes.say: Good. (He shakes your hand, once, firmly. It feels like a contract signed in oak.)

say: (He nods and goes to look at the barrel.)
